summary.text: Andrew "Andy" Beck, a Democrat from West Bend, Wisconsin, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. House seat in Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District to Scott Fitzgerald.
A Milwaukee native, he has worked in hotel management and in sales and management roles in the health care technology industry, and has a background as an MRI technologist.
It was his first run for public office.

paragraphs.text: Beck was born and raised in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and graduated from Washington High School after attending Milwaukee Public Schools, according to his announcement and Ballotpedia survey.

He earned a bachelor's degree in hospitality management from the University of Wisconsin-Stout (1990, per Ballotpedia), a certificate in radiologic technology from the Froedtert School of Radiologic Technology, and an MBA from Cardinal Stritch University (2001, per Ballotpedia).
According to his campaign announcement, Beck held management roles at Hilton Hotels, GE Healthcare and Hologic, and Ballotpedia lists his career experience as sales manager and MRI technologist.
He describes himself as a healthcare professional and business leader, and as the son of Wisconsin's union movement.
Beck lives in West Bend and has lived in the 5th District for over 20 years, according to the Watertown Daily Times.
He announced his candidacy in October 2025 as his first run for public office, and became the Democratic nominee after fellow Democrat Ben Steinhoff withdrew.
During the campaign, his priorities included lowering prescription drug costs, expanding affordable health care, increasing housing construction and protecting democracy.
He received 41.0% of the vote to Scott Fitzgerald's 59.0%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
